value.body: CSR executives manage the social projects that companies fund, usually in education, health, livelihoods or environment. They sit in a company's CSR team or foundation, or in an NGO or consultancy that runs CSR programmes for companies. Work includes selecting partners, field monitoring, budgets and the annual reporting a company's board needs.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA in Sociology or Social Work, BSW, or an MSW

items.label: Legal basis
items.note: Requires eligible companies to spend on CSR and report it

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, MIS dashboards, survey tools, report templates

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start at NGOs or CSR consultancies that implement company programmes, then move into company CSR teams. Many company CSR roles prefer an MSW or a development-studies master's, or two to three years of field experience.

value.title: At a glance
items: Company CSR teams are often small, so openings are limited.
Common next steps: CSR manager, programme manager, or sustainability and ESG reporting roles.
The work sits between business and development, so both sides' language helps.
